about: Element defaults (prompts/DXF2BIM_MODELLER_LANE.md §L18). One entry per setting a 2D layout may not carry. kind 'std' = a value with a named source in this repo or the rate pack; 'guess' = typical practice, to be confirmed. A person states a value with @DEFAULT=<key>,<value> in the drawing (or in the editor / CLI); otherwise the default is used to determine measurements and the row is yellow. A 2D layout carries these only when it comes fully formed from an IFC model.

wall.height.basis: typical storey wall height; not stated by a plan

wall.top_when_unseen.basis: a wall no elevation shows runs from its floor to the slab underside above (the section states it); HHS Level 2 / 3 = the model, Level 1 0.3 m above the model's (its walls stop at a ceiling the drawings do not show); 'none' leaves such walls as asks

slab.outline_when_not_rect.basis: when the walls do not draw a rectangle, the slab is the area they bound on both axes (best effort, amber; HHS -10% against the model's floor slabs, a rectangle +163%); 'none' leaves the slab out and lists it

slab.edge_joint_close.basis: §D70.1 the plan's slab edge closes gaps and notches narrower than this (plank / modelling joints are not drawn: hollow-core joints are grouted monolithic, the open keyway about 3/4 in, Oldcastle Hollowcore Plank Pocket Guide 2019); 0.05 m = the reader's thinnest wall (CFG wall.min_thickness), measured joints <= 24.9 mm (JKR), the first wall gap 60 mm (HHS)

slab.edge_void_min_area.basis: §D70.1 a hole in the slab is drawn as an opening when at least a 254 mm (10 in) square: the producer shows openings larger than 10 in square on shop drawings, smaller ones are core-drilled in the field (Oldcastle Hollowcore Plank Pocket Guide 2019); a hole a column or wall drawn on the same plan fills (>= 0.9) is that element, never an opening

slab.underside_when_stepped.basis: when the section's slab under a level steps (finish on planks, a dropped wet area), the underside is the stack bottom under the longest cut (best effort, amber; JKR with STR: 84.33 under 77% of the cut); 'none' leaves it a conflict

synth.slab.footprint.basis: the slab edge is taken at the outermost grid lines of the base plan

synth.roof.sheet_thickness.basis: display thickness of a roofing sheet (1 in); the cost is by area

synth.roof.overhang.basis: the roof is cut at the gable planes until an overhang is stated

roof.slope_deg.basis: typical light roof pitch; used only when no gable or section gives the slope

door.height.basis: typical door set height; plans do not draw it

door.thickness.basis: typical leaf thickness for a leaf drawn as one line

door.operation_standard.basis: the running standard of a 2D set's doors whose operation the model does not state (F7 D18): the majority side of the building's stated single-swing doors; drawn yellow on A-DOOR-DFLT

door.width.basis: typical single leaf; used only for a door tag with no drawn swing or gap

window.width.basis: typical window width; used when a plan symbol gives no width

window.sill.basis: typical sill height above the floor

column.size.basis: square section when a column symbol gives none

column.height.basis: storey height when no elevation gives it

beam.width.basis: section width when no label or band gives it

beam.depth.basis: section depth when no label or band gives it

footing.length.basis: pad footing plan length when no schedule gives it

gradebeam.width.basis: grade beam width when no label gives it

stair.riser.basis: typical riser height; a stair symbol carries no riser

ceiling.thickness.basis: board thickness when a ceiling is implied

pile.length.basis: no pile length is drawn on a layout

plate.thickness.basis: 1/4 in, the thickness the truss section's own label states (a plate with no label takes it)

member.size.basis: square envelope for a member with no label or size

fan.depth.basis: housing depth; the diameter is drawn

net.thickness.basis: netting sheet thickness; the area is drawn

panel.plane.basis: an elevation panel is placed on the outermost grid line of its face, centred

section.spacing.basis: a section drawn once repeats at the column pitch from its cut

building.type.basis: the kind of building; it selects the type-specific defaults and organises the reference component library. A person states it (@DEFAULT=building.type,Farming Shed)

synth.column.belowgrade.size.basis: 0 = not stated: no below-grade column is built; state the schedule's below-grade section (e.g. 0.3556 for 14 in)

synth.column.grade_to_base.basis: grade to the column base (plinth): 2 ft, the datum read from a column detail

type.size_tie.basis: a size the library answers with several types (Duplex 819 x 759: SMALL_FIXED, CASEMENT) binds the library's first row (8 of the Duplex IFC's 12 are that type); an explicit binding or label always wins; 'none' leaves such fills as asks

slab.level_step_min.basis: slab tops closer than this are one level (the measured finishes are 25-50 mm); a step of this size or more is drawn as its own piece with its own top and thickness (A-FLOR-OTLN elevation / thickness, A-FLOR-LEVL line); 1 or more = one level per storey

slab.edge_arc_sagitta.basis: an arc in a slab edge is read as straight facets no further than this from the arc (5 mm: under the reader's thinnest wall and the plank keyway)

profile.angle_mesh.basis: a section bar whose label states one equal-leg angle (1.5"x1.5"x1/4" Angle) is built as that L section (t(2b-t) x length) instead of its b x b box; 'box' keeps the drawn prism

profile.angle_heel.basis: which way an angle opens is not stated by a section label; the heel corner sits at the low side of the bar's normal (the b x b envelope is kept either way)

fan.blades.basis: the drawing's rings give the housing and hub radii, not the blades; a propeller fan is drawn with this many radial paddles

fan.housing_wall.basis: the housing is a tube of the drawn outer radius; its wall is not drawn

General.about: no type-specific overrides: the base defaults apply

Farming Shed.about: poultry / livestock sheds: open-sided or tunnel-ventilated houses with brick low walls, wire net above, gable-end fans, evaporative pads, outward-opening doors. Bangladesh broiler houses are 'open sided natural house' with cross-ventilation through wire net (SAU lecture); wide tunnel houses add end fans and pads.

door.height.basis: Farming Shed: preferred door 6 x 2.5 ft opening outward (TNAU)

door.width.basis: Farming Shed: preferred door 6 x 2.5 ft (TNAU)

synth.roof.overhang.basis: Farming Shed: roof overhang at least 3.5 ft to keep rain out (TNAU)

never_copy.IfcFan: fan count is an airflow sizing for the new length, not a repeat
never_copy.IfcDoor: doors are placed by use, not per bay

bay_repeat.basis: normal practice for a uniform-bay farm / industrial shed: it is lengthened by whole bays, each new bay repeating the typical bay's frame, side wall, purlins and sheets at the same pitch (owner 2026-10-27/28, DXF2BIM_FOUNDATION_LANE.md §D89 / §D90)

typical.note: ranges for plausibility advisories, never ground truth
